name: Procyanidin oral (melasma)
summary: An antioxidant pill combo with one small placebo-controlled melasma trial reported, and little else.
lead: Oral procyanidin combined with vitamins A, C and E is a supplement regimen that has been tested for melasma, a facial hyperpigmentation disorder. Wikipedia's melasma article lists it among oral options, citing an 8-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 56 Filipino women with epidermal melasma .

name: Quinine skin lightener
summary: An antimalarial alkaloid reported in illicit lightening products, with no studies of it for skin tone.
lead: Quinine has been reported as an ingredient in some skin-lightening products sold illegally, alongside corticosteroids, mercury compounds and bleach-based preparations . Wikipedia's skin whitening article mentions it in the context of a 1997 Paris police crackdown on illegal trafficking of such products .

name: Lead-based ceruse
summary: A historical lead-based white face paste that whitened skin and poisoned its users.
lead: Ceruse, also called Venetian ceruse or white lead, was a cosmetic paste of lead carbonate used for centuries to whiten the face and cover blemishes, scars and freckles, often prepared with vinegar. Pale skin signalled wealth and leisure in the societies that used it, since outdoor labourers tanned.

name: Pearl extract
summary: A traditional pearl-derived brightening ingredient with a 2,000-year pedigree and mostly lab-level evidence.
lead: Pearl extract and pearl powder are preparations made from pearls or nacre, used in traditional Chinese medicine and in cosmetics marketed for brightening and anti-aging. Pearl medicine in China has a history of more than 2,000 years, and it is described as used to calm the mind, clear the eyes and soothe skin.

name: Fermented rice water (sake lees)
summary: Pressed sake residue used in J-beauty masks for brightening, backed by user reports and a tyrosinase-inhibitor finding.
lead: Sake lees, known in Japanese as sake kasu, is the white pressed residue left after sake is drawn from fermented rice mash; it typically contains around 8 percent alcohol. It is used in Japanese cooking and, in skin care, in face masks, bath powder and creams marketed for brightening and moisture.

name: Citric acid
summary: A common food acid and cosmetic pH adjuster that is also an AHA peel ingredient, with little skin-specific trial data.
lead: Citric acid is a weak organic acid found naturally in citrus fruits and an intermediate in the Krebs cycle. It is widely used as a food acidulant (E330 in the EU) and, in cosmetics, as a pH adjuster; it is also classified as an alpha hydroxy acid and is an active ingredient in some chemical peels.

name: Trichloroacetic acid peel
summary: A medium-depth clinical peel acid studied in small trials for photodamage, melasma and acne, with real burn and scarring risk.
lead: A trichloroacetic acid (TCA) peel is a chemical peel using TCA, a strong acid, to cause controlled injury and shedding of the skin; it is described as a medium-depth peel usually done in a doctor's office or outpatient surgery centre. It is used for photodamage, pigment disorders such as melasma, acne and scars, and actinic keratoses.

name: Lactobionic acid
summary: A lactose-derived sugar acid sold as a gentle, humectant 'PHA' in skincare, with plenty of chemistry and transplant-medicine use but almost no published skin trials.
lead: Lactobionic acid (LBA) is a disaccharide sugar acid formed from galactose linked to gluconic acid, and can be made by oxidising lactose. It is freely soluble in water and forms salts with calcium, potassium, sodium and zinc.

name: Gluconolactone
summary: A food-additive-turned-skincare 'PHA' that small trials suggest irritates less than glycolic acid, though the evidence base is thin.
lead: Gluconolactone, also called glucono-delta-lactone (GDL), is the cyclic ester of D-gluconic acid, made from glucose oxidation. It is approved as a food additive (E575) used as an acidifier, sequestrant and leavening or curing agent.

name: PHA (polyhydroxy acid)
summary: A marketing and chemical category of larger-molecule exfoliating acids (gluconolactone, lactobionic acid) pitched as the gentle cousins of AHAs, with sparse trial data.
lead: Polyhydroxy acids (PHAs) are a group of organic acids that carry multiple hydroxyl groups and are used in cosmetics as mild exfoliants and humectants. The two usually named are gluconolactone and lactobionic acid. Gluconolactone is the lactone of gluconic acid, an oxidised derivative of glucose, and lactobionic acid is a gluconic acid-galactose disaccharide.

name: Willow bark extract
summary: A salicin-rich herbal extract with some oral trial data for back and joint pain, but essentially no trials as a skin ingredient.
lead: Willow bark extract is a preparation from the bark of willow trees, most often white willow (Salix alba), containing the glucoside salicin along with polyphenols. Salicin was isolated in crystalline form in 1828, and salicylic acid is derived from it chemically.

name: Birch sap
summary: A spring-tapped tree water used traditionally as a tonic and hair or freckle wash, now appearing in K-beauty serums; skin evidence is mostly lab-level.
lead: Birch sap, also called birch water, is the liquid tapped from birch trees such as Betula pendula and B. pubescens during the spring thaw. It is clear, slightly sweet and consumed fresh or fermented across boreal regions.

name: Erythromycin topical
summary: Old-school topical macrolide antibiotic for acne, labelled for that use only.
lead: Topical erythromycin is a macrolide antibiotic applied to the skin, most commonly as a 2% solution, whose US-labelled indication is the topical treatment of acne vulgaris. It acts against skin bacteria such as Propionibacterium acnes (now Cutibacterium acnes), and reviews of topical acne antimicrobials list erythromycin alongside clindamycin as commonly used agents.

name: Minocycline foam
summary: Prescription minocycline foam trialled in Phase 3 for acne (4%) and rosacea (1.5%).
lead: Topical minocycline foam is a prescription formulation of the tetracycline antibiotic minocycline, developed to deliver the drug to the skin while limiting systemic exposure. A 4% foam (FMX101) was studied for moderate-to-severe acne vulgaris, and a 1.5% foam (FMX103) for papulopustular rosacea.

name: Ivermectin cream
summary: Prescription antiparasitic cream approved for rosacea bumps, backed by Phase 3 trials.
lead: Ivermectin 1% (10 mg/g) cream, marketed as Soolantra, is a topical antiparasitic approved for papulopustular rosacea. It is applied once daily to the face.

name: Quassia amara extract
summary: Herbal 4% gel tried in two small studies for rosacea and seborrheic dermatitis.
lead: Quassia amara is a tropical shrub of the Simaroubaceae family whose extracts have been reported to have antiparasitic and anti-inflammatory properties. A topical gel containing 4% quassia extract has been tested in small clinical studies in rosacea and facial seborrheic dermatitis.

name: Cimetidine for acne
summary: An old stomach-acid drug with weak antiandrogen activity that was tried for acne decades ago, with little supporting evidence.
lead: Cimetidine is a histamine H2 receptor antagonist developed at Smith, Kline & French in the 1970s to reduce stomach acid, and it is sold in many countries for ulcers and heartburn. Because it has a weak ability to block androgen receptors at high doses, it has occasionally been tried as an off-label treatment for acne, both by mouth and as a topical lotion.

name: Chlormadinone acetate pill
summary: A European antiandrogenic progestin in combined birth-control pills, used for acne in some countries with little published acne-specific trial data found.
lead: Chlormadinone acetate (CMA) is a synthetic progestin with antiandrogenic activity, used in combined oral contraceptives with ethinylestradiol such as Belara, which is sold in Germany and Brazil. Because it blocks androgen receptors and lowers LH and FSH, such pills are used in some countries for androgen-related skin conditions including acne and hirsutism.

name: Drospirenone pill
summary: An antiandrogenic birth-control progestin that is indicated for moderate acne in some regions, with most published research focused on PCOS.
lead: Drospirenone is a progestin and antiandrogen related to spironolactone, patented in 1976 by Schering AG and introduced as a combined pill with ethinylestradiol around 2000. It is sold as Yasmin, Yaz and generics, and is also used in progestin-only and estetrol combination pills. Wikipedia notes the low-dose ethinylestradiol/drospirenone pill is indicated for moderate acne in some jurisdictions, alongside premenstrual disorders.

name: Ruxolitinib cream
summary: A prescription JAK-inhibitor cream approved for vitiligo repigmentation and eczema, backed by phase 3 trials.
lead: Ruxolitinib cream (brand name Opzelura) is a topical Janus kinase (JAK1/JAK2) inhibitor. The US FDA approved it in September 2021 for mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, described as the first topical JAK inhibitor approved in the US, and in July 2022 for vitiligo. Its appearance relevance lies mainly in vitiligo, an autoimmune condition that causes skin depigmentation.

name: Tapinarof
summary: A prescription AhR-agonist cream for psoriasis and eczema with phase 3 support; seborrheic dermatitis use is not yet backed by trials found.
lead: Tapinarof (brand name Vtama) is a 1% topical cream and an aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) agonist. The US FDA label lists it for plaque psoriasis in adults and atopic dermatitis in adults and children aged 2 and older. Its mechanism in these conditions is described on the label as unknown, although laboratory work shows it binds and activates AhR in skin cells.

name: Roflumilast cream
summary: A prescription PDE-4 inhibitor cream and foam approved for psoriasis, eczema and scalp or facial seborrheic dermatitis, with phase 3 data for psoriasis and eczema.
lead: Roflumilast cream (brand name Zoryve, developed by Arcutis) is a topical phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE-4) inhibitor. The US FDA approved the 0.3% cream for plaque psoriasis in July 2022, a 0.3% foam for seborrheic dermatitis in December 2023, and a 0.15% cream for atopic dermatitis in July 2024. Seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis are visible skin conditions, which is the basis of its appearance relevance.

name: Sofpironium
summary: Prescription topical anticholinergic gel for underarm sweating; trial-backed for hyperhidrosis, not a cosmetic.
lead: Sofpironium bromide is a topical anticholinergic gel developed by Bodor Laboratories and licensed to Brickell Biotech for primary axillary hyperhidrosis (excessive underarm sweating). It is designed to reduce sweating by blocking M3 muscarinic receptors in eccrine glands at the application site. It received its first approval in Japan in September 2020 under the brand name Ecclock.

name: Dexpanthenol
summary: Vitamin B5 derivative in soothing, barrier-support skincare; studied mainly for wound healing and irritation.
lead: Dexpanthenol (also panthenol, provitamin B5) is the stable alcohol analog of pantothenic acid (vitamin B5). Pantothenic acid is a component of coenzyme A and is described as essential to normal epithelial function; topical dexpanthenol is used on skin because it penetrates well and reaches high local concentrations. It appears in barrier-supporting and soothing skincare products, often as a humectant at concentrations of a few percent.

name: Calendula extract
summary: Marigold flower extract used in soothing skincare; studied for wound healing, with no appearance-specific trials found.
lead: Calendula extract is a preparation from the flowers of Calendula officinalis, used in topical skincare and traditional wound-care products. Laboratory studies have reported anti-inflammatory properties for flower extracts, and human and animal studies have examined it mainly for wound healing.

name: Ciclopirox shampoo
summary: A prescription antifungal shampoo with several vehicle-controlled trials for scalp seborrheic dermatitis and none for hair growth.
lead: Ciclopirox shampoo is a medicated shampoo containing the synthetic hydroxypyridone antifungal ciclopirox, used mainly to treat seborrheic dermatitis of the scalp, a common inflammatory condition that causes flaking, redness and itching and overlaps with ordinary dandruff. Ciclopirox is a broad-spectrum antifungal with reported anti-inflammatory properties and is active against Malassezia yeasts, which are implicated in seborrheic dermatitis.

name: Climbazole
summary: An azole antifungal found in anti-dandruff shampoos; research in the sources is mostly environmental, with little clinical data to cite.
lead: Climbazole is a synthetic imidazole antifungal used as an active ingredient in over-the-counter anti-dandruff shampoos, lotions and conditioners, and sometimes as a preservative. It belongs to the same azole class as ketoconazole, clotrimazole and miconazole and is active against Malassezia yeasts thought to contribute to dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis.

name: Coal tar shampoo
summary: An old-school tar-based dandruff and psoriasis shampoo with trial support for scalp flaking and long-running carcinogenicity debates.
lead: Coal tar shampoo is a medicated shampoo containing coal tar, a viscous dark by-product of coke and coal-gas production, sold over the counter for dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis and scalp psoriasis. Wikipedia notes that patient acceptance is limited because tar products can stain, smell strongly and be messy.

name: Glycerin
summary: The ubiquitous humectant in moisturizers and cleansers, with long use but no cosmetic trials in the sources reviewed.
lead: Glycerin (glycerol) is a colorless, odorless, sweet-tasting, viscous sugar alcohol that is miscible with water and hygroscopic, meaning it draws in moisture. It is one of the most common ingredients in skin care, hair care, soaps, shaving products and personal lubricants, where it functions as a humectant and gives a smooth feel.

name: Lanolin
summary: A wool-derived emollient wax in lip balms and moisturizers, with allergy history and trials aimed mainly at sore nipples.
lead: Lanolin is a yellow, waxy substance secreted by the sebaceous glands of wool-bearing animals, mainly sheep, and recovered from wool washing; it is often called wool fat or wool wax although it is mainly sterol and wax esters rather than a true fat. Purified lanolin is a widely used emollient in skin care, lip balms, baby products and nipple creams, and it resembles lipids of human skin.
